To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) The initial charm quark distribution in nucleus-nucleous collisions at RHIC can be described by the mini-jet model, but at the LHC the initial charm production is underestimated.

the initial yield of charm quarks in heavy-ion collisions at RHIC can be estimated using the mini-jet model, while at LHC secondary production of charm quarks is significant and has to be included in the calculation of the total charm production.

the initial heavy quark yields are in reasonable agreement with PYTHIA and the mini-jet model, that the secondary charm production in the quark gluon plasma is negligible for RHIC and significant for LHC, and that leading order processes cannot reproduce the measured elliptic flow for charm quarks at the RHIC energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of heavy quark pairs in heavy ion collisions.
the investigation of the initial and final state production of heavy quark in high-energy nuclear collisions.
the production and the elliptic flow in nucleus-nucleous collisions at RHIC as well as the production of charm quarks in nucleus-nucleon and proton-nucleon collisions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heavy quark production in the quark gluon plasma is still not fully understood.

at RHIC the charm production in the initial hard process is the dominant source of heavy quarks, while for LHC charm and bottom quarks are produced both in initial hard collisions and secondary in the QGP.
charm quark production at LHC can be described within a mini-jet approach, but that at RHIC the mini-jet model has to be extended to higher order processes to explain the elliptic flow.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the production of charm quarks is dominated by the leading order mini jet production.
the elliptic flow data of charm quarks is well reproduced by the partonic transport approach.
the charm quark elliptic flow at RHIC and the total charm cross section at LHC are well described within the partonic transport approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the elliptic flow at RHIC can be explained by a combination of leading order and higher order processes in BAMPS, while at LHC higher order processes dominate.
the elliptic flow at RHIC is mainly due to charm quarks produced via secondary production processes.

heavy quark production and flow at RHIC are mainly determined by the initial mini-jet production, but that for LHC charm quarks are produced also in the plasma and that the elliptic flow is dominated by the interactions in the plasma.
